patch.why: Design and verification (12-24 months for a rad-hard SoC, general) compress several-fold; fabrication (3-4 months per run), scarce heavy-ion beam time and, for traditional space parts, QML-class qualification (1-2 years) do not. Orbital compute adds a funded commercial customer with no certifying regulator, which raises the odds of an AI-designed space accelerator, but credit to agentic EDA for an Nvidia or Tesla part is unlikely to be disclosed. First tape-out in 2029-30 under S2; flight qualification of traditional rad-hard parts after 2031. Chain (S2): research-grade math public 2027 -> AI multiphysics design with guarantees and agentic EDA (cap-design-optimization, 2028) plus agent-written hardware proofs (verif-hardware-proof-agents, 2028) -> a radiation-tolerant SoC designed and formally verified 2028-29 -> tape-out (3-4 months per run) and heavy-ion test 2029-30 -> credited first silicon 2030 (Medium; disclosure of the AI share is the main risk).

revisions.reason: framework rule: tier 5-7 outcome by 2031 needs its chain written out

patch.why: Robotic powder synthesis is now cheap and repeatable; with reliable characterization and trustworthy screening, discovery rates can rise roughly tenfold. The node stacks two criteria: independent replication, which needs other groups to synthesize and characterize the material (6-18 months), and a >10x rate for which no agreed baseline exists; High is defensible only for replication alone, so S2 is Medium. For space, the first beneficiaries are materials made by simple routes (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes), not superalloys or ceramic composites whose processing autonomous labs cannot yet do. Chain (S2): applied math public 2027 -> reliable automated characterization (2027) and atomistic models with trustworthy error bars (2028) -> autonomous labs at scale (2028) -> candidate materials synthesized 2028-29 -> independent replication 6-18 months later, so first credited discoveries 2029-30 (Medium).

revisions.reason: framework rule: tier 5-7 outcome by 2031 needs its chain written out

patch.why: Algorithms are ready by 2028-29 in S2; space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator are the gates, and US civil SSA funding is under pressure (Office of Space Commerce FY2027 request down about 80%). Screening tens of cislunar objects uses ordinary propagation, so certified million-object screening, provably safe coordination protocols and a certified stability atlas improve the service but do not gate it. A basic military or commercial service is plausible by 2031. Chain (S2): certified collision-probability math 2028 -> cislunar tracking with honest uncertainty in chaotic dynamics (astro-cislunar-od-uq, 2028) -> algorithms ready 2028-29 -> space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator, which AI math does not supply -> a basic service 2031 (Medium).

With validated availability models arriving in 2029 (S2), sites committed afterwards cannot sell an SLA before 2030. Scheduling tools for ground stations already exist and accelerate this node rather than gate it. Chain (S2): applied math public 2027 -> validated optical-link availability models (comms-optical-availability-models, 2029) -> sites chosen and committed 2029 -> 18-36 months of construction across about ten sites -> a weather-robust service with an SLA from 2030 (Medium).

patch.why: Inspection is a large part of reuse cost: non-destructive testing of large structures is slow and access-limited (ONERA, 2026). patch.title: Seeing farther: space science and Earth observation
patch.thesis: If AI can do the theory, inference and instrument mathematics behind missions, science return per dollar rises from existing archives by 2028 and big-telescope design work gets cheaper. Flight dates do not move: LISA still launches in 2035, BHEX cannot fly before about 2032, and HWO moves at the pace of appropriations (FY2027 request: $5M, down from $150M). The one lane where an observatory can fly sooner is privately funded, such as Schmidt Sciences' 3 m Lazuli (target 2028), and there the physical clock, not AI, sets the date. Warp drives get sharper no-go theorems, not engines. The branch also carries Earth observation, absent before v3: honest error bars on methane and ground-deformation retrievals (S2 2028, Medium), while regulators using satellite methane numbers as compliance evidence is only Low by 2031 in the base case.
